Subject: MAP: Data policy milestone — acceptance checklist and owners

Thanks again for the time today, Sarah — great conversation. Per our call, attached is a first-pass Mutual Action Plan focused on the data-handling milestone you asked us to clarify. I pulled out the specific acceptance criteria you emphasized (retention, audit trails, and PHI controls) so we can move the procurement/legal review in parallel with the pilot.

Quick summary / ask:
- I attached HealthSyn_MAP_v1.xlsx (tab: Data Policy). Please review the milestone rows and confirm if the proposed acceptance criteria match your expectations.
- Can you confirm the internal owner at HealthSyn who will sign off on the audit-log sampling? I noted Audrey Chen as the point on our call but want a final name for the MAP.
- Proposed target for milestone completion: 2026-12-10 (pilot-ready + audit evidence). If that won't work, share any hard blockers.

Key MAP excerpt (data-policy milestone):
- Owner (Redwood): Ben Carter — deliver configuration and sampling instructions.
- Owner (HealthSyn): [TBD] — verify retention windows and sample audit logs.
- Acceptance criteria:
  • Retention windows configurable to 30/90/365 days
  • Audit trail shows: request id, timestamp, model version, requester id for sample set
  • PHI/PII handling: data classification enforcement and optional redaction at ingest
  • KMS-backed key management for persistent artifacts
- Dependencies: SOC2 summary for security baseline (attached), legal MSA redlines, and network peering completion.

Next steps I suggest: you confirm the internal owner and any additional acceptance tests by end of day Friday (11/12). I’ll then update the MAP and loop Ben and Monica in for technical and compliance detail.

Attachments: HealthSyn_MAP_v1.xlsx, SOC2-Summary.pdf

Neha — thanks for the recap and the clear checklist. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Internal owner: Audrey confirmed she will be the primary owner for sign-off on the audit sampling, but she asked that our Head of Data Governance (TBD in parallel with legal) also be looped for final acceptance. I’ve CC'd Audrey.

2) Acceptance tests: We’d like an additional bullet that the audit-sample will include both anonymized and non-anonymized records (we need to validate redaction is reversible for debugging, but only accessible to a small ops group).

3) Retention: 30/90/365 windows are fine, but we also need an option for retention=0 (ephemeral) for specific ingestion pipelines ingesting strictly PHI — call that out as a must-have.

4) Evidence: For procurement, Legal wants a short (1–2 page) evidence note describing how audit logs are generated and where they are stored (encrypted at rest) — can your team produce that?

Happy to sync on a 30-min call this week if that helps.

Cheers,
Sarah
Sr. Product Ops, HealthSyn Therapeutics

Quick technical reply and commitments below. Attaching an annotated doc (retention-reqs-annotated.docx) with detail.

Extraction and sampling:
- Approach: we will provide an API-based log pull that can emit structured audit entries (JSONL) for any requested time window. For small proof-of-evidence requests we can also provide CSV exports.
- Sample contents: request_id, timestamp (UTC), model_version, route, requester_id (hashed by default). For reversible PHI debugging we support a reversible tokenization mode gated by RBAC and only available to a named ops group.

Retention=0 (ephemeral) pipelines:
- Implementation: ephemeral pipelines omit persistent blob writes; they keep transient KV cache with TTL <= 24 hours and no disk-backed artifacts. We will add a policy flag and enforcement tests to the infra CI.

Encryption/KMS:
- All persistent artifacts (when enabled) are encrypted with customer-managed keys (CMK) via our KMS integration. Audit logs uploaded to the customer storage bucket are server-side-encrypted; we will include the KMS key id and a short proof-of-config in the audit-evidence-note.

Deliverables and dates (confirmed):
- Ben: technical runbook + sample extraction script + example CSV — 2026-11-19
- Monica: evidence note draft + compliance checklist — 2026-11-22
- Neha / Lauren: MAP updated with HealthSyn owners + send for sign-off — 2026-11-24

I flagged a small dependency: to demonstrate reversible tokenization we need a test dataset with <= 1,000 PHI-labeled records and a signed data transfer agreement. If HealthSyn can provide that by 11/17 we can include reversible samples in the 11/19 deliverable.

Attachments: retention-reqs-annotated.docx
